Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.
data.title: F1: Follow-detection mechanism research spike

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want income to accrue only to the owning player of each placed business and shared events/incidents to retain their existing semantics routed per-owner, so the competitive economy is legible and testable.

## Context

`applyIncome` / adjacency income and `resolveEvent`/`resolveIncident` are single-player (one resourceBank/finalScore). Once street slots are owner-tagged (state-model sibling) and the phase machine delegates Income/Incident to per-owner handlers, the routing must be precise. Incident/Investment event regression risk: silent divergence where the wrong owner is credited or both are affected.

## Scope

- Per-owner income: each placed business's income (base + adjacency + upgrades + salary/ongoing) accrues only to its slot owner.
- Shared events/incidents: street-wide Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified (design within planning: per-owner effects vs. shared board effects).
- Single-player (N=1) income path unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Phase machine / win condition (sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Income for each placed business accrues only to the owning player (verified by per-owner fixtures covering base + synergy + upgrade + salary/ongoing).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics and are routed per-owner as specified (design within planning); verified by per-owner event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic replay: same seed → identical per-owner income/event sequences.
- [ ] **AC4:** N=1 regression: income/event behaviour matches the pre-competitive single-player baseline.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner `applyIncome` variant, shared event/incident routing.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Per-owner income computation helpers.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-income-events.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive income/event tests (per-owner fixtures, shared-event routing, determinism, N=1 regression).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model (owner-tagged slots) + shared-day phase machine (closing-phase delegation)
- Required by: competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — ownership-aware scoring) + Monte Carlo harness
data.title: Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution

# Feature: Deterministic Banking AI Tests (BankingGreedyStrategy)

## Summary
Expand `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` to contract `BankingGreedyStrategy` (distinct class, not `GreedyStrategy`) for hoard/spend/cap/legality/difficulty; leave Greedy baseline untouched.

## Target Outcome
Deterministic, fast unit tests prove `BankingGreedyStrategy` deliberately hoards vs spends correctly and respects legality, before implementation lands.

## Definition of Done
- Suite imports `BankingGreedyStrategy` (name === 'BankingGreedy', implements MainStreetAiStrategy) alongside unchanged Greedy/Random.
- Cases: (a) hoards (end-turn with actionsRemaining>0) when an unaffordable high-value hand/market target exists, (b) spends when no valuable unaffordable target, (c) at bankedActions==2 returns spend (bank value 0), (d) respects enumerateLegalActions legality (no illegal action emitted), (e) difficulty scaling — Easy spends where Hard hoards on same state.
- Existing ai-action-budget + monte-carlo tests remain green (or drift documented).
- `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New suite targets `BankingGreedyStrategy`; GreedyStrategy and RandomStrategy remain importable/unchanged.
2. Deterministic hoard vs spend vs cap vs legality cases covered (a–d above).
3. Difficulty scaling test: same state, Easy spends where Hard hoards (or quantified threshold difference documented).
4. No regression in existing ai-action-budget / monte-carlo tests (or documented drift).

## Minimal Implementation
- Retarget/create helper makeState({hand, market, coins, banked, difficulty/config}) in tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts.
- Table-driven tests for cases above; include helper to build MainStreetState with hand/market/business+upgrade/event cards and bankedActions.
- Run: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`.

## Dependencies
None (test-first — blocks F2).

## Deliverables
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (expanded/retargeted)
- Passing unit run for touched file

## Key Files
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts`

## Constraints
- Main Street only; no core-engine changes.
- Do not modify GreedyStrategy behaviour in this slice — tests define the contract it must satisfy in F2.

# Add turn cost to card and scoring tooltips

## Problem statement
The per-turn ongoing cost (`ongoingCost`) of cards is not consistently displayed on card tooltips and is entirely absent from the score calculation tooltip, leaving players unclear about the true cost of maintaining their businesses.

## Users
- **Players of Main Street** — When evaluating whether a business card is worth purchasing, players need to see both the one-time cost and the ongoing per-turn cost. When viewing their score, they need to understand how ongoing costs affect their final score.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **Card tooltips**: The `ongoingCost` (turn cost) is consistently displayed for **all card types that have it** (Business, Community Space, Staff) — shown even when the value is 0, using the format `Ongoing cost: -0/turn` for zero-value and `Ongoing cost: -{N}/turn` for non-zero values.
2. **Score tooltip**: The score tooltip includes a total ongoing turn cost line computed from all placed Business, Community Space, and Staff cards (sum of their `ongoingCost` values).
3. **i18n**: New score tooltip strings use i18n keys registered in `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` (`MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`).
4. **Tests**: Unit tests verify `buildCardTooltipInfo()` includes the turn cost line for all applicable card types, and `buildScoreTooltip()` includes the turn cost breakdown.

## Constraints
- Changes are scoped to Main Street example game (`example-games/main-street/`).
- Follow existing formatting conventions (`formatCurrency`, i18n keys, `
`-separated tooltip lines).
- No changes to game logic, rules, or card data — purely UI/display changes.

## Existing state
- **Card tooltips** (`MainStreetFormatting.buildCardTooltipInfo()`):
  - Business: shows `Ongoing cost: -{ongoingCost}/turn` **only when > 0**
  - Community Space: shows `Ongoing cost: -{ongoingCost}/turn` **only when > 0**
  - Staff: shows `Ongoing cost: -{ongoingCost}/turn` **only when > 0**
  - Event/Upgrade: no ongoing cost (correct, they are one-shot)
- **Score tooltip** (`MainStreetHudTooltips.buildScoreTooltip()`):
  - Shows coins, reputation, challenges breakdown
  - No turn cost information at all

## Desired change
1. Update `buildCardTooltipInfo()` to always show the ongoing cost line for applicable card types (Business, Community Space, Staff), even when the value is 0.
2. Update `buildScoreTooltip()` to include a total turn cost line computed from all placed cards' `ongoingCost` values.
3. Add appropriate i18n keys for the new score tooltip strings.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `buildCardTooltipInfo()` — Always show ongoing cost line
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildScoreTooltip()` — Add turn cost breakdown
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` — Add new i18n keys
- `tests/` — Tooltip unit tests (or `example-games/main-street/tests/`)

## Related work
- CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7: Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover
- CG-0MQK1UDDC0027MKQ: Settings should only show tooltips switch if they exist

## Risks & assumptions
- **Assumption**: "Turn cost" refers to the `ongoingCost` field (per-turn maintenance cost), not the one-time purchase cost.
- **Assumption**: This is scoped to Main Street only (not other example games).
- **Risk**: Showing `Ongoing cost: -0/turn` on every card may add visual clutter. Mitigation: the line is short and follows the existing format; players who care see it, those who don't ignore it.
- **Scope creep**: Consideration of showing turn cost as part of AI decision-making or economic analysis tools is out of scope.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers
*(None — proceeded based on codebase context)*
data.title: Add turn cost to card and scoring tooltips

# Feature: Design architecture & extraction script with history (F1)

Decide the target multi-repo layout, enumerate assets, and build the history-preserving extraction script. Full history preservation via `git filter-repo` is required (per producer).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Architecture decision recorded: core repo contents (`src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards`, Gym, launcher shell `src/ui/GameSelectorScene` + `src/ui/createCardGame`, `electron/`, shared configs), game repo layout as sibling `tce-<game>` dirs, launcher composition via `configs/*.json` presets and a Vite discovery plugin.
2. History-preservation strategy confirmed as `git filter-repo` and the exact filter commands / script are documented and dry-run verified.
3. Asset ownership enumerated case-by-case for `public/assets/` — audit of `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and per-game usage; decision table committed (which assets stay in core vs move with a game).
4. Extraction script `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (or equivalent) produces the core-engine directory/repo and 8 per-game scaffolds from the current monorepo state with history preserved; dry-run output is verifiable.

## Technical Notes

- Use `git filter-repo` (not subtree/manual squashed history) — producer confirmed full history preservation.
- Enumerate shared vs per-game assets before any moves; thumbnail assets are per-game (each game provides its own).
- Sibling layout: core at `../tableau-card-engine-core` relative to each `tce-<game>` sibling.

## Key Files

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (new)
- `docs/extract-architecture.md` or decision record (new)
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
- `public/assets/**`

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Full history preservation? A (producer, this session): yes, via `git filter-repo`.
- Q: Asset ownership? A (producer, this session): enumerate in F1, decide case-by-case.
- Q: Dynamic discovery approach? A (producer, this session): convention (GAME_INFO per game) is fine; per-game thumbnails.
- Q: Post-build dynamic addition? A (producer, this session): rebuild sufficient for now; Electron runtime plugin is a follow-up (core-version compatibility required).

# Staff business-type matching engine

## Summary
Add allowedBusinessTypes CSV column, update existing staff cards, and create matching helper functions for business-type validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV column**: allowedBusinessTypes column added to all staff rows in `card-data.csv`. Format: comma-separated list of specific business names and/or synergy type names (e.g. a Barista lists `Cafe`, a generalist lists broad types such as `Food,Culture,Service,Commerce,Entertainment,Health`).
2. **Existing staff updated**: ~20 existing staff cards receive allowedBusinessTypes where natural specialisation exists (e.g. Barista -> Cafe). Hand-slot staff (Assistant, Manager, Director, Executive) get broad type coverage. Specialist staff (Bookkeeper, IT Specialist, Health & Safety Inspector, etc.) get targeted type lists.
3. **New specialist rows**: New specialist staff cards added with allowedBusinessTypes + income-buff effects (e.g. Florist -> Florist with income bonus).
4. **Matching helpers**: `staffMatchesBusiness(staff, business, state)` helper function that checks if a staff's allowedBusinessTypes matches the business's name (exact) or any of its synergyTypes.
5. **State model**: BusinessCard extended with employedStaff: StaffCard[] array for per-business staff tracking.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add allowedBusinessTypes?: string[] field to StaffCard interface in MainStreetCards.ts
- Parse allowedBusinessTypes from CSV in loadStaffTemplates()
- Implement staffMatchesBusiness() helper that matches against business name (exact) or synergy type (via synergyTypes)
- Add employedStaff: StaffCard[] to BusinessCard interface
- Update getEmployedStaffCountAt() to use new field instead of filtering state.staffCards
- Backfill existing employedAtSlot references during deserialization (migration)

## Deliverables

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` -- updated staff rows with allowedBusinessTypes
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` -- interface extensions, matching helpers
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` -- employedStaff field, deserialization migration
- Unit tests: CSV schema validation, business-type matching (name + type), state model integrity

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts`
- `tests/main-street/staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` (new)
